key_insight: A graph-based reinforcement learning architecture coordinates global and node-level control while preserving permutation symmetries and transparency constraints.
engineering_relevance: The framework supports network-wide resource budgeting and local allocation, with applications to capital interventions in interconnected financial institutions.
method: Use a message-passing neural network with separate global and local policy heads.
Derive explicit Lipschitz bounds for input and parameter perturbations.
Use these bounds to establish convergence guarantees for projected policy-gradient optimization.
evidence_signal: Financial-network experiments report better performance than feedforward neural-network baselines and scalability to large networks, though the abstract provides no quantitative results.
watch_item: Sensitivity and optimization behavior depend on architecture and graph characteristics, so robustness should be checked for each target network.
paper_title: Reinforcement Learning for Global-Local Control of Dynamic Networks with Applications to Systemic Risk
